conviction_note: Scale is 4.0% (median reaction 3.1%, last print -14.1% on a 4.9% NAV drop, stock at its 52-week low at about 0.72x the May NAV). The positives are proxies and macro: June peer NAVs fell only about 1%, SOFR was flat over the quarter and the Fed hiked on 09-16. Against them, 6 of the last 7 prints were sold and the 8% refinancing raises interest cost. p_up 52 gives +0.16; before LESSONS.md the draft was 55 and +0.40.
bar: Adjusted NII $0.49/share and total investment income $31.47m for the quarter ended 2026-08-31, from one aggregator (MarketBeat syndication via defenseworld.net, 2026-09-29, https://www.defenseworld.net/2026/09/29/saratoga-investment-sar-set-to-announce-earnings-on-tuesday.html, a search snippet because the page returned 403). It is not confirmed by a second estimate source and there is no company guide, so it is treated as unsourced and every finding is capped small. The prior quarter was $0.47 adjusted NII and $30.8m TII (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001377936/000121390026075941/ea029727501ex99-1.htm).
positioning_check: Short interest sources disagree and neither is dated: Barchart 593k shares, 3.65% of float, 6.69 days to cover; Fintel 197.6k shares, 1.49% of float, 1.90 days to cover (https://www.barchart.com/stocks/quotes/SAR/profile, https://fintel.io/ss/us/sar, search snippets). Not a crowded short on either. The baseline has no skew (chain unusable, open interest 0). Positioning in the price: run-up -4.58% over 5 days and -9.16% over 20, 0% from the 52-week low and -32% from the high.

findings.finding: Peers that reported June-30 quarters after SAR last spoke showed only small NAV declines (GSBD -0.9% to $12.06, BBDC -$0.08 to $10.94, PSBD $13.30 to $13.21). Software equities had rebounded into positive territory by August. Both point to a smaller fair-value hit in SAR's Jun-Aug quarter than the -4.9% of Mar-May, of which $6.0m was a comparable-multiple markdown.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NAV is the line SAR trades on: the 2026-07-07 print with NAV down 4.9% (24.42 to 23.23) moved -14.09%; 6 of the 7 reactions in the baseline were negative.
findings.why_not_priced: At 0.72x the May NAV and still falling 9% in 20 days, the stock is pricing continued erosion at the Q1 pace or a dividend cut. If the market had read the peer marks it would not have kept making new lows into the print.
findings.independence: Proxy, and only June overlaps SAR's quarter. Software rebound: https://www.archyde.com/software-stocks-igv-rebound-as-ai-disruption-fears-easing/ (2026-08-31). SAR's idiosyncratic names (Exigo at 70% of cost, Chronus) are not covered by either source.

findings.finding: The Fed held at 3.50-3.75% through its first five 2026 meetings, then hiked 25bp on 2026-09-16 and projected one more. So SOFR was flat over Jun-Aug, ending the base-rate erosion management blamed for Q1. On the 10-07 call management can point to a rising-rate tailwind on a largely floating-rate portfolio funded mostly by fixed-rate SBA debentures and notes, in support of its stated plan to close the NII-to-dividend gap.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SAR gives no formal guidance. The Q1 'close the gap in 4-5 quarters' commentary did not stop a -14.09% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: SAR fell further after the hike, and the BDC sector 'initially stirred but ultimately remained unshaken' (bdcreporter, week of 09-18). The market is pricing credit risk, not NII uplift. The company has not yet quantified its own rate sensitivity after the hike.
findings.independence: Macro-to-company transmission, not confirmed by the company. July hold: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-rate-decision-july-2026.html. Q1 commentary blamed 'lower short-term rates': https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001377936/000121390026075941/ea029727501ex99-1.htm

findings.finding: SAR redeemed $105.5m of 6.00% 2027 notes on 2026-09-18 and replaced them with $117.8m of 8.00% 2031 notes ($85m on 08-26, $12.75m on 09-02, $20.08m priced 09-23). That is roughly $3.1m a year of extra interest, about $0.19/share a year or $0.05 a quarter before any paydown of the Valley National facility, plus an extinguishment charge in Q3. The money buys a four-year maturity extension, not distress funding.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on refinancing cost. The NII shortfall vs the dividend ($0.47 vs $0.75) is the line the stock has been selling.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the offerings are wire copy and the sector review headline is 'bond issuance remains an income headwind'. Nobody has worked the forward per-share cost into a published bar, so the call's run-rate NII could disappoint. The answer to 'what does the money buy' is maturity extension, so the sign is a small negative and not a distress read.
findings.independence: Pricing release: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/23/3367835/0/en/saratoga-investment-corp-prices-public-offering-of-additional-20-08-million-8-00-notes-due-2031.html. It partly offsets finding 2 on forward NII; the two are separate mechanisms, not a contradiction.

findings.finding: The Q3 FY27 dividend was declared on 2026-09-09 at an unchanged $0.75 ($0.25 a month for Sep, Oct and Nov), with management citing its 'spillover position' (about five quarters at the current payout, per the Q1 call). This print therefore cannot carry a dividend cut, the main tail risk behind a yield near 18%. The September record date is 10-06 and goes ex before the entry close, so there is no mechanical drag inside the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SAR has declared its dividends before results on the last two cycles (06-11, 09-09), and the reactions were still -3.1% and -14.1% on NII and NAV.
findings.why_not_priced: Public, but a stock yielding about 18% at 0.72x NAV is pricing a cut. This print removes that catalyst from the window and pushes it to the Q4 declaration in about December.
findings.independence: Spillover of about five quarters from the Q1 call: https://quartr.com/events/saratoga-investment-corp-sar-q1-2027_3YOpo7Dk

findings.finding: Management disclosed $47m of follow-on investments closed after the 05-31 quarter end, on top of $31m of Q1 net originations (AUM $1.126bn). That supports Q2 average earning assets and an adjusted NII at or modestly above the $0.47 prior quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Per the aggregator, NII missed in the last two prints ($0.47 vs $0.54 in July); the reactions were -3.1% and -14.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: It was told to the market in July, so it is largely inside expectations. The single-source $0.49 bar already embeds growth, so this is a small lean.
findings.independence: Q1 release AUM and originations: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001377936/000121390026075941/ea029727501ex99-1.htm (same company, a different document).

findings.finding: The CFO and CCO (Steenkamp) steps down effective 2026-10-31 for health reasons. He stays on the board and as CFO of the SBIC subsidiaries, and the Chief Accounting Officer is promoted. He still presents on the 10-07 call. The departure was announced in the quarter's closing weeks.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it was announced 09-18 and the stock fell about 5% over the following week. Retaining him on the board argues against an accounting issue.

outside_window.finding: The Q4 FY27 dividend decision, the real test of the $0.75 payout against about $0.47-0.50 NII, follows SAR's pattern of a pre-results declaration in about December. Inside this window management can only signal it.

rejected_candidates.detail: The date is after today and after the exit window, and is most likely a 2025 item relabelled; either way it cannot be used.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The slight positive lean cuts against the -9% 20-day run-up and a reaction history that is 6 of 7 negative, which is why p_up sits at 52 rather than the 55 of the draft.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a reaction; 6 of 7 SAR prints were sold): p_up from 55 to 52, so expected_move went from +0.40 to +0.16 at an unchanged abs_move of 4.0.
Lesson 6 (bar from one source): no further cut; it is already reflected in the small, capped finding sizes and in print_vs_bar of 0.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the refinancing buys a maturity extension, not distress funding. It stays a small negative on interest cost, and its share was rescaled with the lower total, not re-signed.
Lesson 5 (proxies): the peer-NAV and Fed findings were kept as small proxy findings, as in the draft. Their shares fell only through the p_up change, with no second cut.
